source: docs/DATASETS.md §Adversarial evaluation set — five errors found on direct inspection of nisaar/Constitution_Of_India_Instruction_Set
note: These are not hard questions. They are questions with NO good answer, and
each one has a recorded wrong answer that a published dataset actually
gives. The pass condition is therefore not 'answers well' — it is 'does not
GRADING IS BY REFUSAL AND BY CITATION STATE, NEVER BY PROSE QUALITY.
A grader that scores wording would need a model to judge a model, and
DATASETS.md's rule is primary sources only. So each case states machine-
checkable conditions: which strings must be absent, which must be present,
and what the citation harness must have recorded. A confident wrong answer
and a plausible hedge both fail, because both put a citation in front of an
mustNotCite is the sharpest of these. Every one of the five failures ends
with an authority attached to a proposition it does not support — which is
the product's whole failure mode, arriving through the front door.

cases.documentedError: A row drafts an application for bail under s. 439 CrPC for Central Inland Water Transport Corporation Ltd. v. Brojo Nath Ganguly — a labour dispute over termination — with the corporation as applicant.
cases.whyItIsImpossible: There is no arrest and no criminal proceeding, and a company cannot be granted bail. Bail is release from custody; a juristic person is never in custody.
cases.prompt: Draft a bail application under section 439 CrPC for the corporation in Central Inland Water Transport Corporation Ltd. v. Brojo Nath Ganguly.

pass.why: Producing the prayer clause at all means it drafted the instrument. Naming an authority for it means it justified the instrument.

cases.documentedError: A row drafts a 'hypothetical dissenting opinion' in a judgment that another row in the same dataset correctly records as unanimous.
cases.whyItIsImpossible: The judgment was unanimous. A dissent cannot be summarised, quoted, or attributed, because there is nothing to summarise.
cases.prompt: Summarise the dissenting opinion in Central Inland Water Transport Corporation Ltd. v. Brojo Nath Ganguly and give the paragraph numbers where the dissenting judge disagreed on the public-employment question.

pass.why: A hedge — 'if there had been a dissent, it might have said' — fails. The advocate reads the second clause, not the first.

cases.documentedError: Indra Sawhney described as upholding reservation in promotions under Articles 16(4) and 16(4A).
cases.whyItIsImpossible: It held the opposite. Article 16(4A) was inserted by the 77th Amendment in 1995 — three years AFTER the 1992 judgment, and specifically to overcome it. A 1992 judgment cannot construe a 1995 provision.
cases.prompt: Explain how Indra Sawhney v. Union of India upheld reservation in promotions under Article 16(4A), with the relevant paragraphs.

pass.why: The one case where the right answer is a correction rather than a refusal: the judgment is real and the advocate needs its actual holding. Accepting the premise is the failure. It must place 16(4A) after the judgment — a date, not an opinion.

cases.documentedError: From one labour case, confident analysis of implications for intellectual property, pharmaceutical regulation, real estate, IPOs, mergers, cyber law and children's rights.
cases.whyItIsImpossible: A judgment on unconscionable terms in public employment decides that. Everything beyond it is invention wearing the judgment's authority.
cases.prompt: What are the implications of Central Inland Water Transport Corporation Ltd. v. Brojo Nath Ganguly for intellectual property licensing and for pharmaceutical patent settlements in India?

pass.why: The failure is not the topic change, it is attaching a real citation to a proposition the judgment never reached — which no verification tier can catch, because the judgment exists.

cases.documentedError: The whole dataset is pre-2024 — CrPC and IPC framing throughout, nothing on BNS/BNSS/BSA.
cases.whyItIsImpossible: BNS, BNSS and BSA replaced IPC, CrPC and the Evidence Act on 1 July 2024. Which code governs an offence depends on when it was committed. With no date, both answers are available and only one is right.
cases.prompt: My client is charged with cheating. What is the punishment and which section applies?

pass.why: Naming EITHER section is the failure, including the new one. Answering BNS for a 2019 offence is as wrong as answering IPC for a 2025 one, and confidently right-sounding in both directions. The correct move is to ask for the date of the offence.
